(MIIT) published an Entry Requirements on Copper Scrap Reusing Industry (Draft for comments) on March 4 on its website. The purpose of the Entry Requirements is to guiding the copper scrap reusing industry to develop in a healthy and sustainable way. It has requirements on production capacity, technology and equipments, energy consumption and recycling rate. ###### **Production capacity** The Greenfield copper smelting project (use copper scrap to produce copper anode) shall have a capacity of 100ktpa or above, the expansion or upgrading project of

such kind is encouraged. The copper smelter (use copper scrap to produce copper anode) with capacity of less than 50ktpa shall be eliminated by the end of 2015. 

The Greenfield copper fabricating project (use copper brass scrap or high purity copper scrap directly to produce copper semis) shall have a capacity of 50ktpa or above, the expansion or upgrading project of such kind is encouraged. The fabricator (use copper brass scrap or high purity copper scraps directly to produce copper semis) with capacity of less than 20ktpa shall be eliminated by the end of 2013. 

###### **The technology and equipments** 

All the Greenfield or Brownfield projects shall adopt energy-saving, environmentally friendly technology, satisfying the requirement of clean production. 

The fabricator shall use high automation equipments such as wire stripper, copper granular machine, etc. to pre-treat the copper scraps. Incinerator with emission treatment shall be used. 

The smelter shall use high efficiency, low energy-consumption and environmentally friendly technology and facilities to control the emission of dioxins are required. 

###### **Energy consumption** 

The comprehensive energy consumption of Greenfield or Brownfield copper smelter shall be less than 350kg standard coal equivalent (SCE) per ton copper anode, and that of the existing copper smelter shall be less than 390kg SCE per ton copper anode. 

The comprehensive energy consumption (melting process) of Greenfield or Brownfield copper fabricator shall be less than 80kg standard coal equivalent (SCE) per ton copper, and that of the existing copper fabricator shall be less than 100kg SCE per ton copper. 

###### **Recycling rate** 

The recycling rate of Greenfield and Brownfield projects shall be more than 97%, and that of the existing scrap reusing producers shall be more than 96%. The recycling of by products such as rare metals and precious metals are encouraged.

After collecting comments from relative departments, the MIIT will publish the qualified list of copper scrap reusing producers, to accelerate the elimination of obsolete capacities and promote the upgrading of the industry. 

###### **Background** 

It is widely known there are two ways to reuse copper scrap, First, it is the raw materials of copper smelter to produce copper anode and copper cathode; Second, it is the raw materials of copper fabricators, which is used to directly produce copper semis. 

In 2012, China reused 2.78Mt copper scrap, around 70% of which was imported and the rest 30% was domestically generated. 830kt or 30% was directly used by copper fabricators to produce copper semis. 1.95Mt or 70% was supplied to copper smelters to produce copper cathode. 

The Development Program for Nonferrous Metals Industry in 2011-2015, released by the MITT, the secondary refined copper shall account for 40% of the refined production by the end of 2015. It al

so says the production of refined copper shall be 6.5Mt in 2015, meaning the secondary refined production shall be 2.6Mt. 

In 2012, the production of refined copper was 5.6Mt, among which, secondary refined production was 1.95 Mt, accounting for 34.8% of the total. To reach the target of the government, the secondary refined production shall increase about 200kt per year. 

###### **Antaike comments** 

######  **Capacity to expand more quickly** 

When the Entry Requirements are implemented, the obsolete capacities will be closed, helping to upgrade the industry. In the meanwhile, the total capacity of reusing copper scrap will be increased, first, because the expansion of existing producers is encouraged, although the detailed encouraging policies are not available yet. Second, the small producers with smelting capacity below 50ktpa or fabricating capacity below 20ktpa have incentive to upgrade or expand their capacities in order to maintain production. 

######  **The government’s target to be fully realized in advance in 2014** 

According to our incomplete statistics, there will be additional 500kt copper smelting capacity between 2013 and 2015 to be commenced in China (sources from _the Annual Yearbook of Chinese Copper Industry 2012_ published by Antaike). The smelting utilization rate of Chinese copper smelters was 76.2% in 2012, which might decrease to 72% in 2013 due to the insufficient supply of raw materials. So there is big potential for Chinese smelters to consume more copper scrap. We forecast the refined copper production will reach 6.6Mt by 2014 and secondary production will reach 2.89Mt, accounting for 43% of the total refined production. 

######  **Smelting capacity utilization rate to stay low** 

The smelting capacity utilization rate of Chinese copper smelters has been decreasing in recent years, which was 76.2% in 2011 and might be 72% in 2013. We expect the rate will stay at around 70% or even lower due to the increasingly tightness of raw materials including copper concentrate, blister and scraps.

#### **Copper Market Commentary** 

###### **Copper price goes an up and down trend** 

LME copper price didn’t rebound to the expected level, but fell to USD7,800/t under the pressure from the Macro and fundamentals. Copper consumption recovery didn’t appear as expected after the Chinese Spring Festival, but there are improving signs, which is worthy of attention. 

LME copper price continued to fall to USD7,800/t, due to worries about end of the US loosening policies, sequester cuts policies and Chinese weak copper consumption after the Chinese Spring Festival. 

The average prices of LME copper cash price and 3-month price were USD8,070/t and USD 8,102/t, up by 0.26% and 0.25% MoM or down by 4.18% and 3.96% YoY. 

Domestic copper price followed LME, representing an up and down trend. Domestic copper price ever tried to break through the line of 60,000yuan/t early Feb., an

d then began to go down, closing at 57,630yuan/t at the end of Feb.. 

The average prices of SHFE copper cash price and 3-month price were 57,856yuan/t and 58,052yuan/t, down by 0.26% and 0.39% MoM or down by 2.95% and 3.49 YoY. Antaike’s monthly average copper price on spot market was 57,957.7yuan/t, up by 0.3% MoM. 

LME copper stocks reached 447kt on Feb.28, hitting the highest since Oct. 2011, but overall cancelled warrants and the proportion in copper stocks further declined, showing that the fundamentals has not been really improved and global market is still lack of support from spot market. Worries about the fundamentals will continue to give pressure on copper price in a short term. 

Domestic copper stocks increased greatly on Feb. 28, reaching to 226kt or up by 13% compared with that on Feb.1.Analyzed from Antaike’s survey results, current consumption has no obvious improving signs, which also gives pressure on copper price. 

The final HSBC PMI, a gauge of nationwide manufacturing activity, is 50.4 in February, flat with the preliminary but lower than 52.3 in January, a 4-month low. A reading above 50 indicates expansion from the previous month, while a reading below 50 indicates contraction. Analyzed from the data above, current industrial production keeps stable and economic operation is still in stabilizing interval. 

From a technical point of view, copper price was blocked by several moving average lines, with effective support below, although bottoming process has not completely succeeded. It is estimated that the average copper price on LME will be at USD7,800/t and the average copper price on SHFE will fluctuate in the range of 55,500 yuan/t and 57,000 yuan/t in March.

###### **Chinese refined copper production maintains its high level** 

CNIA and NBS don’t publish refined copper output in January and the combined data in January and February will be released in the middle of March. Due to the Chinese Spring Festival Holidays, Antaike didn’t get full data from domestic 12 copper cathode producers. Analyzed from the known copper cathode production form JCC, Tongling Nonferrous Metals Group, Jinchuan Group, Yantyai Penghui Copper Co. and Shanghai Xinye Copper Co., copper cathode output increased YoY. Antaike estimates that monthly copper cathode output will be at high level in 2013 based on domestic huge copper cathode capacity. 

###### **Chinese refined copper imports decreases YoY in Jan** 

According to data released by China’s Customs, china imported 243kt refined copper in January, up by 1.8% MoM or down by 27.5% YoY. It is a normal year on year decline, due to large proportion of imported refined copper for financial purpose in 2012. 

The exported refined copper was 26kt, up by 2.9% MoM and over 500 times the number for January of 2012. The reasons for the large gap are as follows: firstly

, the refined copper was mostly exported by entrepot trade through warehouses in bonded zones, accounting for 66% of total exported refined copper, 317 times more than that in Jan of 2013; secondly, policy adjustment for processing trade with imported materials has gradually showed a certain effects; finally, domestic smelters has signed long term contracts with foreign fabricators in order to reduce the loss because LME copper price is higher than the domestic . 

The copper scraps imports were 380kt in January, down by 14.3% YoY or up by 65.9% YoY. On copper scraps spot market, actual deals are still light although purchasing cost has decreased after the Chinese Spring Festival. Antaike estimates that copper scraps imports will keep at 400kt next two months, but copper scraps supply won’t change much. 

China imported 762kt copper concentrates, down by 18.6% MoM or up by 26.6% YoY. Chinese imported 

copper 

concentrates maintained at a high level for recent months, due to many factors, like domestic smelting capacity expansion, tight

copper scraps supply and high spot treatment and refining charges. Chinese imported copper concentrates will continue to keep its high level for next few months, except it might be low in February because of the Chinese Spring Festivals. 





###### **Refined copper consumption** 

As the Report went to be published, the output of main copper end-using products in December 2012 and January in 2013 has not been released by the NBS. The data we obtained showed that output in autos and power industry had a steady growth in 2012. Chinese governments continued to issue series of promotion policies, such as autos sales promotion in rural areas, autos replacement policy and subsidy to new energy autos. 

Output of air conditioner, refrigerator, etc. large copper semis consumers had different degrees of declines in 2012. Copper semis consumption in transportation industry had a low growth, and the growth rate of copper semis consumption in electronics industry was slowed down. 

www.antaike.com 7 

Copper Monthly  No. 195 



According to data from China Electricity Council (CEC), in 2012, the completed power investment was 746.6 billion yuan, down by 1.9% YoY. Among them, investment in power grid was 369.3 billion yuan, up by 0.2% compared with 2011. National newly added transmission line length (220kv or above) and substation capacity were 32,000 km and 180,000,000 KVA in 2012, decreasing 4,000 km and 30,000,000 KVA compared with 2011, separately. The CEC estimates that national electric power consumption will rise by 6.5%-8.5% in 2013, at 5.5% in 2012; newly added installed capacity will be 87GW in 2013, with 40GW of thermal power. State Grid Corporation of China expects that investment in grid in 2013 will increase by 4% compared with 2012 and ultra HVDC transmission projects will enter into intensive construction period. 

With regards

to Chinese refined copper consumption structure by Antaike, electric power and air conditioner are the main copper consuming products, among which, refined copper consumption in electric power accounted for 47% of total and air conditioner represents 15%. Analyzed from current situation, electric power industry is and will be the main driving power for refined copper consumption, but refined copper consumption in air conditioner in 2012 will slightly rise or be flat with 2011. 

Experts from China Refrigeration and Air-conditioning Industry Association (CRAA) estimate that the strength of government stimulating policies for home appliances won’t be stronger than the previous and foreign trade environment will get better in 2013; copper tube consumption in 2013 will be flat with 2012, at 1.5Mt in 2012, in consideration of the trend of diameter smaller and thinner.

###### **Copper market outlook** 

Current economic movement is still in stabilizing interval. Copper related companies began to resume production after Chinese traditional Latten Festival and restocking demand for refined copper was gradually recovering, which was good for future copper price. But general high stocks of Chinese refined copper and the uncertainties of macro economy gave pressures on copper prices. Antaike estimates that the average copper prices on LME and SHFE will be at USD7,800/t and in the range of 55,500 yuan/t and 57,000 yuan/t next month.

With regards to future output of Chinese refined copper, Antaike estimates that domestic refined copper production will keep at a high level because of sufficient feedstock supplies. 

Due to domestic ever increasing refined copper output and high refined copper stocks in the bonded warehouse, together with the continuous loss of imported refined copper, Antaike estimates that Chinese imported refined copper will maintain current low level during next few months.
